Hi everyone, welcome back to the channel. Today I want to talk about the year our little bakery almost ran out of money without anyone noticing. We were busy every single morning, the queue went out the door on Saturdays, and I still could not tell you whether we made a profit in any given month. The problem was not sales. The problem was that every receipt went into a shoebox under the counter and stayed there until the accountant asked for it in March. So the first thing we changed was tiny. Every evening, after we closed, I sat down and typed each receipt into one spreadsheet with four columns: date, supplier, amount, and what it was for. It took about ten minutes. That habit alone showed me that flour had gone up by a third and I had never raised a single price. The second thing was sorting the receipts into piles by supplier at the end of each week, because it turned out two suppliers were charging us for deliveries we never got. We asked for the money back and we got most of it. The third thing was a weekly number I could actually feel: how much cash was left after paying for ingredients and wages. If that number dropped two weeks in a row, I would stop and look before buying anything new. Honestly the software did not matter much. What mattered was looking at the numbers while I still remembered what each purchase was. If you run a small food business, start with ten minutes a night and one sheet. You do not need a fancy system on day one, you need a habit you will keep when you are tired. Next week I will show the exact spreadsheet, column by column, and how I check it against the bank export every Friday afternoon. Thanks for watching, and see you then.
